title: Remap alt and ctrl keys, fail when need write @

status.label: Confirm Spanish-layout remapping on current stable
status.detail: The reporter says the @ mapping works in Windows Search and OneNote but produces 2 or nothing in browsers and IDEs on 0.85.1, and suspects the Spanish layout.

judgment.rationale: The report is a Spanish keyboard layout mapping issue: the reporter says the intended @ output works in Windows Search and OneNote but not browsers and IDEs, where 2 or no character appears. The reporter listed PowerToys 0.85.1 in October 2024 and later identified the affected apps and suspected Spanish Windows/keyboard settings. The current version and exact mapping from the screenshot are not stated in text.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.73.0 and shows a key-remapping configuration in a screenshot.
The reporter later says the mapping works in Windows Search and OneNote but not browsers and IDEs, using PowerToys 0.85.1.
The reporter suspects the Spanish Windows interface or keyboard layout may be relevant.
A maintainer requested app names and the reporter supplied them; do not repeat that question.
The issue remains open and labeled Needs-Repro; no linked fix was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask only whether the behavior persists on current stable and which Spanish keyboard/input layout is active; use the existing app-specific results rather than requesting the same app list again.

fix_assessment.rationale: If the current issue persists, Keyboard Manager may synthesize the wrong character for a layout-specific Alt/Ctrl combination or the affected applications may interpret the injected sequence differently. The exact mapping and active layout need confirmation.

proposed_fixes.title: Produce the intended @ character consistently across apps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The remapping may use an Alt/Ctrl sequence whose output depends on the active Spanish keyboard layout or on how browser and IDE input controls process injected keys. The exact mapping is only shown in the issue screenshot.
plan: Confirm the current PowerToys version and the active Windows keyboard/input layout.
Read the existing screenshot to reproduce the exact source and target mapping.
Compare the mapped output in Windows Search, OneNote, one affected browser, and one affected IDE.
If Keyboard Manager generates a layout-incompatible sequence, correct the mapping path and add a regression test for the confirmed layout.
verification: Verify the exact mapping produces @ in the previously affected browser and IDE.
Verify the mapping still works in Windows Search and OneNote.
Verify ordinary 2, AltGr, and Ctrl combinations remain correct for the active layout.

confidence.rationale: The app-dependent output difference and likely Spanish-layout context are useful, but the exact mapping and current release behavior remain unverified.

issue_context.summary: A remapping intended to type @ reportedly works in Windows Search and OneNote but produces 2 or no character in browsers and IDEs.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.73.0 and includes a screenshot of the mapping.
The reporter later confirms the affected apps are browsers and IDEs and reports that Windows Search and OneNote work on PowerToys 0.85.1.
The reporter suspects the Spanish interface or keyboard layout.
inferences: A Spanish keyboard layout or app-specific processing of the injected Alt/Ctrl sequence may explain the difference, but the exact key mapping and active layout are unknown.
issue_context.analysis: The prior request for affected app names was answered. The remaining discriminating evidence is the current PowerToys version and active keyboard/input layout; do not ask for raw logs before a current reproduction.
initial_investigation: Read all five comments and the report, including the maintainer's request for affected apps and the reporter's answer.
No linked fix or exact covering issue was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether the issue persists on current stable and the exact Spanish keyboard/input layout active when the mapping is used
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether a current defect remains and whether the wrong output follows the layout rather than the application alone.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the current PowerToys version, Windows display language and active keyboard/input layout, and confirm whether @ still fails in one browser and one IDE while working in Search or OneNote.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that the mapping works in Windows Search and OneNote but not browsers and IDEs, and for noting the Spanish-layout possibility. Could you confirm whether this still happens on current stable, and share the active Windows keyboard/input layout and the exact source/target shown in the screenshot?
